creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`rad check` reports an error on the `epoch` tutorial that `rad docs examples/epoch` ships. The corpus's most-used working script, `cct` at 1103 runs, carries 13 hints. Both review sources reached the same conclusion independently: users learn to skim the hint tier, and then the tier stops working.

Four confirmed false positives, all cases where the surrounding code proves the hint wrong:

- `read_file(...).content` types as `str|int[]` and isn't narrowed by the default `mode="text"`. `refineBuiltinReturn` is the extension point, but it currently sees only positional argument types, so narrowing on a literal kwarg needs literal-type tracking. Sites: `msh:240`, `peer:156`, `htree:182,199`.
- `index_of` returns `int?` and isn't narrowed by an `in` membership guard, so `idx + 1` fires RAD30002 on code that provably can't be null. Hit ~10 times in one script from a single `args.index_of(flag)` flag-parsing idiom.
- Lockstep `sort()` erases element types. It's declared `(_primary: list|str, *_others: list|str) -> list|str` because it sorts strings too, so a destructured capture keeps a `str` possibility that fails any `list`-typed parameter. Three-list capture reports `dynamic|null` instead. Single capture is clean and indexing is unaffected, so it's specifically builtins declaring `list`. The script that hit this kept an unsorted copy under a second name purely to satisfy the checker.
- `.map()` results type as `map|list` (`notes:30`); `[".."] + children` types as `str[] + list|str` (`zook:95`).

The #129 fix in v0.11.0 (`9d986d86`) shows the class is tractable.

This is also a precondition for the migration tooling. Nobody adopts `--fix` on the strength of a diagnostic tier they've been trained to ignore.

---

### Orientation

- All four false positives live in `rts/check/`, which owns the static checker. `rts` must not import `core`.
- Two extension points. `rts/check/type_check.go:2744` `refineBuiltinReturn` sharpens a builtin's declared return type for a specific call site. `rts/check/narrow.go` holds the flow-sensitive narrowing, keyed on Symbols in a Frame.
- Signatures are not written in Go. They come from `docs/funcs/*.md` via codegen into `rts/signatures_gen.go`, so a fix expressed as a narrower signature means editing markdown and running `make generate`.

### Where to start

Per false positive, all four premises verified:

- **`read_file(...).content` typing as `str|int[]`.** The signature is `read_file(_path: str, *, mode: ["text", "bytes"] = "text") -> error|{ "size_bytes": int, "content": str|int[] }` (`docs/funcs/read_file.md:7`). The card's diagnosis is exact: `refineBuiltinReturn` builds its argument list from `tc.positionalArgTypes(call)` (`rts/check/type_check.go:2756`, defined at `:2788`), which walks `call.Args` only and never touches `call.NamedArgs`. Narrowing on `mode="text"` needs the kwarg's *literal value*, which is the literal-type tracking the card names. `rts/check/check_lit.go` is where literal handling already lives.
- **`index_of` not narrowed by an `in` guard.** The signature is `index_of(_subject: str|list, _target: any, *, n: int = 0, start: int = 0) -> int?` (`docs/funcs/index_of.md:7`). `rts/check/narrow.go:190` handles `rl.OpIn` for exactly one shape: `identInStringList`, meaning `ident in [<string literals>]`. Relating `if flag in args` to a separately-bound `idx = args.index_of(flag)` means teaching the narrower a guard whose subject is a *different expression* than the symbol being refined. This is much the largest of the four - scope it deliberately, and consider splitting it out.
- **Lockstep `sort()` erasing element types.** The signature is `sort(_primary: list|str, *_others: list|str, *, reverse: bool = false) -> list|str` (`docs/funcs/sort.md:10`). The `sort` arm of `refineBuiltinReturn` (`rts/check/type_check.go:2761`) refines only `len(args) == 1` and deliberately leaves the parallel form at the wide type - the code comment explains that parallel sort returns a list-of-lists, not `args[0]`. The refinement for the multi-arg case is therefore "a tuple of the argument types", not "args[0]".
- **`.map()` typing as `map|list`, and `["..."] + children` typing as `str[] + list|str`.** `map`'s signature is `map(_coll: map|list, _fn: fn(any) -> any | fn(any, any) -> any) -> map|list` (`docs/funcs/map.md:7`). Same allow-list; the refinement is "returns the collection kind it was given".
- Read the allow-list's own comment before extending it (`rts/check/type_check.go:2736-2743`): "This is a deliberately tight allow-list, not a general mechanism - resist growing it without a concrete need." Four concrete needs is the argument for growing it. Make that argument in the commit message.
- Precedent worth reading first: `9d986d86` "fix(check): stop false positives on valid scripts (#129-131, #133)".
- Related lever already in place: `rts/check/check.go:146` `strictOnlyCodes` demotes RAD30011 to `--strict` only, with a comment recording that it was ~73% of all hints in a real-script sweep. If a hint cannot be made precise, that table is the alternative to leaving it noisy - but keep it small, as its comment says.

### How to verify

- `make build`, then `./bin/radd check script.rad`.
- The tutorial the card names ships from `docs-web/docs/examples/epoch.md` and is served by `./bin/radd docs examples/epoch`.
- Checker snapshots live in `rts/check/snapshots/`, notably `builtin_refine.snap` and `narrow/`. Update with `go test ./rts/check/ -run TestCheckSnapshots -update=builtin_refine` (the `=` is required; a bare `-update` swallows `-run`).
- Unit tests: `rts/check/type_check_test.go`, `rts/check/narrow_test.go`, `rts/check/narrow_interp_test.go`. Run `go test ./rts/check/`.
- `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go:102` `TestDocSnippets` runs every snippet in `docs-web/docs/` through the checker with per-snippet tolerance entries. Grep that file for tolerances covering these shapes before starting, and remove the ones that become unnecessary.
- `make all`.

### Done when

- Each of the four shapes checks clean, with a case under `rts/check/snapshots/` pinning the refined type.
- The negative cases are pinned too: `read_file(p, mode="bytes").content` still types as `int[]`, and `sort()` over a genuinely mixed input keeps the wide type.
- No tolerance entries left in `core/testing/docs_snippets_test.go` for the false positives that got fixed.
- `./bin/radd check` on the script from `docs-web/docs/examples/epoch.md` reports no diagnostics.

### Watch out for

- `rts` must not import `core`.
- Signatures live in `docs/funcs/*.md`. If a fix is best expressed as a narrower signature, edit the markdown and run `make generate` - `rts/signatures_gen.go` is generated output.
- `refineBuiltinReturn` is conservative on purpose. Widening it wrongly makes the checker miss real errors, which is a worse failure than hint noise. Every refinement needs a matching negative snapshot case.
- The `index_of` item is a different size class from the other three. Landing three of four is a better outcome than stalling on the fourth; if it gets deferred, split it onto its own card rather than leaving this one open.
title: Stop the checker firing hints on provably-safe code
